inApp: TLS to the Yayatoh API and the payment page, from the operating system
Ed25519 signature verification of ticket codes (ticket-crypto) so the door can admit offline
SQLCipher (AES-256) for the encrypted guest list (expo-sqlite)
XChaCha20-Poly1305 for the cache, the outbox and the vault files
Keys kept in the iOS Keychain and Android Keystore (expo-secure-store)
exportCompliance.classification: Mass-market encryption item, ECCN 5D992.c, self-classified (EAR 740.17(b)(1)) because the apps use standard algorithms for data protection beyond the operating system. Standard algorithms only, no proprietary cryptography, no encryption for third parties.
exportCompliance.annualReport: A self-classification report to BIS and the ENC Encryption Request Coordinator is due each year by 1 February for items exported in the year before.
exportCompliance.france: Apple handles the French declaration with the documents uploaded in App Store Connect; nothing is added to the app.
exportCompliance.owner: pending owner and counsel: confirm the classification, upload the documents in App Store Connect, then set IOS_ENCRYPTION_COMPLIANCE_CODE in the EAS environment. Until then each upload asks the export question once per build.

apple.why: A work tool for event teams with no user-generated public content, no web access and no sensitive themes.

2.1.answer: Demo access: a door-device enrolment link and a ticket code, with steps in the review notes. Organizer and exhibitor accounts need an invitation, which the review contact sends on request.

5.1.1.answer: The camera is used only to read QR codes; no images are stored or sent. A door device has no personal account.

3.1.1.answer: The app sells nothing and has no in-app purchase.

play.targetAudience: 18 and over (event staff); not designed for children
